correctness.rationale: Independent Klein-model check: in each half-sector 0 <= theta < phi=pi/n the side is reached at tanh r = cos(phi)/cos(theta). Thus the area inside radius t per half-sector is the integral of cosh(min(t,r))-1. For t above the inradius split at B_n; integrating the side-limited part by v=sin(theta)/sin(phi) yields arcsin(sin(B_n)/sin(phi))=G_n. This gives both CDF branches, the normalized continuous density (including the junction) and the exact incircle mass. Expanding the forbidden half-angle gives B_n(rho+h) ~ sin(phi)*sqrt(2h/cos(phi)); integrating the missing polar area gives exactly the stated h^(3/2) coefficient. At fixed n the allowed angle is 4n*cot(phi)*exp(-2t)+O_n(exp(-4t)); integrating the density gives the stated exponential tail. For the limit, set theta=v*pi/n. After area normalization the two cutoffs in the sector integral tend to exp(s) and b/sqrt(1-v^2), with b=2/pi; the minimum is bounded by the disk cutoff. Dominated convergence gives the integral of this minimum on [0,1], which evaluates to the claimed H through and at its join, and has left mass b at the limiting incircle. Its derivative deficit there is b*sqrt(2h)+O(h^(3/2)) and its right survival asymptotic is b^2*exp(-s)/2. No interchange of fixed-n tail and large-n limits is needed. Independent replay /workspace/replay/04.py passed 20 clipped-sector quadratures and six scaled-sector checks; these are finite checks, not the proof. The frozen checks/regular_ideal_polygon.py is present and was inspected, not executed.
